The chain is typecheck && lint && fallow && format:check && test && test:integration, and format:check fails on pre-existing UNTRACKED files (.mcp.json at repo root, seven .planning/research/.cache/*.json) because .prettierignore lacks .planning/. A real fix needs .planning/ added to .prettierignore AND an operator decision on .mcp.json (gitignore it or commit it). CI is unaffected — neither file is tracked.

blockers.description: Git hooks are NOT installed in this checkout. core.hooksPath resolves to /home/acolomba/pi-claude-marketplace/.git/hooks, which contains no pre-commit file, so git commit runs NOTHING. Every commit in this session passed only because agents ran pre-commit manually.

decisions.decision: D-115-01: make orchestrators/import/index.ts production-reachable rather than suppressing it — repoint edge/handlers/plugin/import.ts through the barrel, prune the barrel to what production consumes, delete all eight fallow-ignore WR-01 markers
decisions.rationale: Operator intends to set fallow production:true eventually. A probe showed that under --production the barrel is reported as an unused FILE and all eight suppressions become STALE. Pruning alone does not help — a one-line barrel is still unreachable. Only a real production import is clean under BOTH settings. Landed in f732f0de.

decisions.decision: D-115-03/04: choose the double strategy per module by contract; delete the c8 ignore at import/execute.ts:214 by proving the production default path
decisions.rationale: Real composition measured cheap (every suite under 4s), so speed was not the tradeoff. import/execute.ts has a test-only 4-collaborator ImportDeps seam plus the repo's ONLY coverage pragma; reconcile/apply.ts has no seam and drives the real lifecycle. Forcing symmetry would either re-prove Phase 114 ground or add test-only surface to four production modules. D-115-04 is still OPEN — it belongs to 115-02.

decisions.decision: D-115-07/08/09: exhaustive entry-kind by failure-mode matrix for import and reconcile, all 23 public outcome kinds, each cell asserting the complete aggregated result
decisions.rationale: Operator chose exhaustive over the recommended outcome-complete sample, with the D-20/D-22 duplication tradeoff stated. D-115-08 bounds it: the matrix varies the COMPOSITION's inputs, it does not re-derive lifecycle internals Phase 114 owns. decisions.decision: D-115-10: give addMarketplace, removeMarketplace, and uninstallPlugin the mode-discriminated overload setPluginEnabled already carries, then delete the three unreachable guards at reconcile/apply.ts:204, :312, :369
decisions.rationale: Those guards cannot be covered because the producers always return an outcome in orchestrated mode. result.status is read immediately after each guard, so deleting a guard without narrowing the producer type requires a non-null assertion — silencing the type system exactly where the contract needs enforcing. enable-disable.ts:565 records the same reasoning. Operator-approved DEL-03 exception. STILL OPEN — belongs to 115-05.

decisions.decision: Set workflow.use_worktrees=false and run plans sequentially
decisions.rationale: GSD's isolation guard wanted each executor in its own git worktree, but node_modules/ is gitignored so a fresh worktree has none, and every plan's verify block runs per-file tests. Sequential execution compensates for the lost isolation — no two executors share the tree at once. Reversible with config-set workflow.use_worktrees true.

decisions.decision: Corrected the arrange-marker acceptance criterion in five plans from 'markers equal runtime cases' to 'markers equal case bodies'
decisions.rationale: The 115-01 proving slice found it unsatisfiable: a row table emits several runtime cases from one marked body (that file: 9 markers, 24 cases). A verifier would have reported a false gap on every pair using a table. The unit-testing rule's own text says data rows still use separate phases. Landed in 3c0081e1.

context_notes: Phase 115 is a compliance refactor, not greenfield: seven of eight owner test files already existed and none carried the mandated lowercase arrange/act/assert markers, so every case is a rewrite. The phase's real yield so far has been finding proofs that could not fail. The planting technique — change the thing a proof pins, confirm the test goes red, revert — is now standard in every dispatch and has caught six distinct instances. When a plant stays GREEN, that is a finding: either narrow the case's claim to what it truly discriminates, or add the case that does. Two executors did exactly that and one of them uncovered a caller-side filter that had been shipping untested. Do not let a later executor paper one over.
